Initial charge on P: $Q_0 = C_P V_0 = (10\times10^{-6}\,\text{F})(6.0\,\text{V}) = 60\times10^{-6}\,\text{C}$
When P is connected across Q, charge is conserved and both reach a common potential $V$ (parallel).
$V = \dfrac{Q_0}{C_P + C_Q} = \dfrac{60\times10^{-6}\,\text{C}}{30\times10^{-6}\,\text{F}} = 2.0\,\text{V}$
Charge on Q: $q_Q = C_Q V = (20\times10^{-6}\,\text{F})(2.0\,\text{V}) = 40\times10^{-6}\,\text{C} = 4\times10^{-5}\,\text{C}$
Check: charge on P is $20\,\mu\text{C}$, and $20 + 40 = 60\,\mu\text{C}$, so charge is conserved.
Answer: 4
